newsitem.title: USA: Countdown continues for U.S. spacewoman's return.
newsitem.headline: Countdown continues for U.S. spacewoman's return.

text.p: The countdown continued on Saturday for shuttle Atlantis' mission to collect U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid from Russia's Mir space station.
NASA officials said they had resolved two minor technical problems and everything looked set for a pre-dawn blastoff from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Monday.

Atlantis was scheduled for liftoff during a narrow seven-minute launch window that starts at about 4:54 a.m. EDT (0854 GMT) on Monday. Forecasters gave the shuttle a 70 percent chance of good weather for launch.
The $2 billion spaceship is scheduled to dock with Mir late on Wednesday to pick up Lucid and drop off her replacement John Blaha.
If Atlantis lifts off as planned Lucid will return to earth September 26 after 188 days in space, a record for a woman and the longest space flight by an American.

It will be the fourth time the shuttle visited the Russian station. A small leak in the shuttle's propulsion system was no longer considered a problem and a recently replaced electronics box checked out fine, according to NASA test director John Stealey.
"The launch team has overcome all the adversities that have been thrown at it so far. They are focused and ready for launch," he said.
Lucid, a 53-year-old mother of three, began her tour of duty aboard Mir in March and was due back in August, but Atlantis was running nearly seven weeks late.
The mission, originally scheduled to begin July 31, was delayed because of rocket problems, a scheduling clash and the threat from Hurricane Fran.

Lucid was the second American to live aboard the orbiting outpost and the first of six U.S. astronauts scheduled to continously staff the station into 1998, part of preparations for long-duration missions aboard a U.S. space station to be built starting late next year.

"Not only have I had a good time, but I think we have gained experience on how to deal with a long flight," Lucid said recently. "I've learned a lot from being with the Russian crew. It's just been a great experience."
